what: Hindi accuracy of the models the in-browser recogniser can run, and their speed in a browser

accuracy.method: Each model's 8-bit ONNX files (the same files the browser downloads) were run with @huggingface/transformers 4.3.2 on onnxruntime-node, greedy decoding, language forced to Hindi, on the first 12 clips of the FLEURS Hindi dev split (real speakers, 141 s in total with the bundled sample) plus bolo's built-in hi-short sample (synthesised). Word and character error rates after removing punctuation; no other normalisation. Twelve clips is a small test: read the numbers as 'usable or not', not to the last digit.
accuracy.test_audio: google/fleurs, config hi_in, dev split, first 12 files of the archive (CC-BY-4.0; not redistributed here); server/src/bolo/samples/hi-short.wav

speed_in_browser.method: Headless Chromium 153 on the build machine (4 vCPU Intel Xeon 2.1 GHz, no GPU), demo build, WebAssembly with 4 threads, model files served from a local mirror so download time is excluded. The machine was running other jobs at the time (load average 9 to 13 on 4 cores), so these are pessimistic; a quiet machine or a recent phone will do better. 'session_rtf' is all compute (partials and finals) divided by the audio length; above 1 means the transcript falls behind the speaker.

speed_in_browser.note: These runs were made before partial results were switched off for models that need more than 1.5 s per pass; with that change a slow model spends its time on finals only.

conclusions: Whisper Tiny and Whisper Base (multilingual, 8-bit) are not usable for Hindi: word error rate above 100 %, output mostly in Latin or Urdu script.

Whisper Tiny fine-tuned for Hindi (ARTPARK-IISc/whisper-tiny-vaani-hindi, Apache-2.0) is usable for a demonstration: about 40 % of words wrong on this test. Its model card reports 26 % on the FLEURS test split for the original weights.
All Whisper models decode a fixed 30 s window per pass and ran slower than real time in the browser on this (busy) machine; Moonshine Tiny did not.
